plugins.name: Announcement Bar
plugins.description: One announcement bar at the top of every page: a short message, an optional link, four styles and an optional close button. Edited in the site settings, no third-party requests.
plugins.tagline: One clear announcement bar at the top of every page
plugins.longDescription:
Announcement Bar puts one short message at the very top of every published page: a sale, a holiday closing, a new product or an event. Type it in the site settings and it is live; empty the message and the bar is gone.

Add an optional link, such as "Shop the roast", to a page on your site or any https address. Pick a style that suits your theme: Quiet (dark), Loud (blue), Warm (orange) or your own colour, with text that switches between light and dark by itself to stay readable.

Let visitors close it if you like. A closed bar stays closed in that visitor's browser until you change the message, so a new announcement always gets seen.

It is small and respectful: a few lines of CSS, a tiny script only when closing is enabled, no fonts, images, tracking or third-party requests. The bar is a labelled region with a real, keyboard-focusable close button and escaped text.

It needs only the storage permission, for its settings. Without it, pages are served unchanged.

screenshots.caption: A warm announcement bar with a link above a live page
Close-up: message, link and a close button visitors can use
Message, link, style, colour and close option in the site settings

plugins.name: Cookie Consent
plugins.description: An accessible GDPR cookie banner in Dutch or English, with accept, reject and per-category settings. It remembers the choice and tells other scripts through a data attribute and a DOM event.
plugins.tagline: An accessible GDPR cookie banner in Dutch or English, with no third parties
plugins.longDescription:
Cookie Consent adds a clean, accessible cookie banner to every published page. Visitors can accept everything, reject everything with one equally prominent click, or open the settings and choose per category: necessary, analytics and marketing.

The banner speaks the page's language: Dutch pages get Dutch text, all others English. Write your own text for either language, link your privacy policy, pick a floating card or a full-width bar, and set the background, text and button colours. Button text stays readable on any colour you choose.

The choice is remembered for 180 days in a first-party cookie, so returning visitors never see the banner flash. A small Cookie settings button, or any element with data-cookie-settings, lets visitors change their mind.

Other scripts can wait for consent: the html element carries data-cookie-consent (for example "necessary analytics"), a stride:consent event fires on document with the choice, and window.StrideConsent offers get() and open().

Everything is inline and about 4 KB. No external requests, no tracking of its own. It needs only the storage permission for its settings, and still shows its default banner if that permission is refused.

screenshots.caption: A floating card on a live page, with Accept all and Reject all given equal weight
Settings lets visitors choose analytics and marketing cookies one by one
Text, privacy link, layout and colours are set from the site settings
On a Dutch page the banner speaks Dutch; here as a light full-width bar

plugins.name: Countdown Banner
plugins.description: A bar that counts down the days, hours and minutes to your sale, launch or order deadline, with a button, and hides itself when the time is up.
plugins.tagline: Count down to your sale, launch or order deadline, then step aside.
plugins.longDescription:
Countdown Banner shows a bar that counts down the days, hours, minutes and seconds to a moment you choose: the end of a sale, a product launch, the last day to order before the holidays. Add a button, such as Shop the sale, and pick a colour; the text colour is chosen for you so it stays readable.

Put it at the top of every page, or let it float at the bottom of the screen. The words are available in English, Dutch, German and French. Set the time in your own time zone, and every visitor sees the right countdown wherever they are, summer time included.

When the time is up the bar hides itself, or shows a closing message such as The sale has ended. The clock runs in the visitor's browser, so it stays right without publishing again. Without JavaScript, visitors still see the message and the date it ends.

The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep the countdown. You can skip pages, such as your checkout.

screenshots.caption: A countdown bar at the top of every page, with a button to the sale.
Floating at the bottom of the screen, here in Dutch on a phone.
The settings: message, end time, time zone, button, language, position and colour.

plugins.name: Custom Code
plugins.description: Adds your own code to the head or body of every page: analytics, a verification tag, a chat widget or a font. Choose which pages get it. No theme edits needed.
plugins.tagline: Add analytics, verification tags and widgets to every page. No theme edits.
plugins.longDescription:
Custom Code puts your own snippets into the published pages of your site: in the head, right after the opening body tag, or at the end of the body. It is the easy way to add a privacy-friendly analytics script, a search engine verification tag, a web font, a tag manager or a chat widget.

Choose which pages get the code: every page, only the pages you list, or every page except those. A * at the end of an address covers every page under it, so blog/* means all your posts under blog.

Your code is inserted exactly as you paste it, and each snippet is labelled in the page source, so you always know where it came from. Before saving, the plugin checks for the mistakes that break a page: an unclosed script tag, a whole page pasted in by accident, or code that is too long.

Only paste code from people you trust: it runs for every visitor. The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep your snippets. Changes apply to a page the next time it is published.

screenshots.caption: Snippets land exactly where they belong, and each one is labelled in the page source.
The settings: code for the head and the body, and which pages get it.

plugins.name: External Links
plugins.description: Opens links to other sites in a new tab, adds a small arrow so readers know they are leaving, and sets noopener and optional nofollow for you. No JavaScript.
plugins.tagline: Links to other sites open in a new tab, safely, with a small arrow.
plugins.longDescription:
External Links takes care of every link on your site that points to another website. It opens them in a new tab, so visitors do not lose your page, and adds rel="noopener noreferrer" so the other site cannot reach back into yours.

A small arrow after the link shows readers they are about to leave, and screen readers hear "opens in a new tab". You can also ask search engines not to follow the links (nofollow), or mark them as paid or affiliate links (sponsored).

Your own pages are never touched: links within your site are left as they are, and the plugin picks up your site's domain when you publish. You can also list your other domains, such as a separate shop, so they count as your own. Links you already set to open in a certain way keep that, and domains you name, such as youtube.com, are left completely alone.

Everything happens once, when a page is published: there is no JavaScript on your pages. The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep its settings; refused, it uses the defaults.

screenshots.caption: A reading list where every outside link gets a small arrow and opens in a new tab.
What changes in the page: new tab, noopener, nofollow and a hidden note for screen readers.
The settings: new tab, arrow, nofollow or sponsored, and your other domains.

plugins.name: Image Lightbox
plugins.description: Lets visitors click an image to see it large, with the caption underneath and arrows to browse every image on the page. Works with the keyboard and on phones.
plugins.tagline: Click any image to see it large, with captions, arrows and swipe.
plugins.longDescription:
Image Lightbox lets visitors click an image on your site to see it big, on a dark or light background, with its description as a caption. Arrows, the arrow keys and a swipe on a phone step through the other images on the page, with a counter such as 2 / 4.

It is built on the browser's own dialog, so it works with the keyboard and with screen readers: images that can be enlarged are announced as buttons, Escape closes the viewer, and focus returns to the image you came from. Animations are left out for visitors who ask their device for less motion.

It is careful about what it touches. By default only images shown smaller than they really are can be enlarged, so small icons and decorations are left alone. Images inside a link, the header, the menu or the footer never open, so logos and buttons keep working. You can skip pages, such as your shop.

No libraries and nothing loaded from elsewhere: a small inline script and stylesheet, added only to pages that have images. The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep its settings; refused, it simply uses the defaults.

screenshots.caption: Click an image and it opens large, with its caption and arrows to the next one.
A light background suits a bright, airy site. The counter shows where you are.
On phones, swipe to the next image and tap to close.
The settings: which images, captions, arrows, background and pages to skip.

plugins.name: Instant Pages
plugins.description: Makes clicking around your site feel instant: pages start loading while a visitor points at a link, and fade smoothly into each other. No scripts.
plugins.tagline: Pages load while visitors point at a link, and fade in smoothly.
plugins.longDescription:
Instant Pages makes moving around your site feel instant. When a visitor rests the pointer on a link, the browser quietly prepares that page; when they click, it is already there. Pages then fade into each other instead of flashing white.

It uses two features built into modern browsers, Speculation Rules and View Transitions, declared in two small tags. No script of ours runs and nothing is sent to anyone. Browsers without these features simply work as before.

It is careful. Addresses that do something when visited, such as signing out, checkout, the admin and the API, are never loaded early, and neither are links that open in a new tab, download a file or carry a search query. You can add your own addresses to that list, and choose to start loading only when a link is pressed, to save data.

Visitors who ask their device for less motion get a plain change between pages. The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep its settings; refused, it uses the defaults.

screenshots.caption: Point, prepare, click: the next page is ready before the visitor clicks.
The settings: when to load, how much, the change between pages and what to skip.

plugins.name: Maintenance Mode
plugins.description: Shows visitors a polished coming-soon or maintenance page while you build, with an optional launch countdown and contact line. Signed-in editors still see the real site.
plugins.tagline: A polished coming-soon page for visitors while editors see the real site
plugins.longDescription:
Maintenance Mode puts a clean, full-screen coming-soon or maintenance page in front of your site while you build it. Visitors see the placeholder; you and your editors, signed in to Stride, keep seeing the real pages, with a small badge reminding you that the curtain is up.

It works with zero configuration. Optionally add your site name, your own headline and message, a launch date with a live countdown, and a contact line. An e-mail address becomes a link. Choose a dark or light look and an accent colour; text keeps its contrast whatever you pick. Dutch pages get Dutch default text.

It fails closed: the page is hidden before any script runs, so visitors without JavaScript never see the site. A noindex tag keeps search engines from indexing the placeholder. The countdown is accessible, animation respects reduced motion, and nothing is loaded from third parties.

It needs only the storage permission, for its settings. Refuse it and the default maintenance page still shows. Note that this hides the site, it does not lock it: the real HTML is still in the page source.

screenshots.caption: Visitors see a dark coming-soon page with the launch date, a live countdown and a contact link
Signed-in editors keep seeing the real site, with a small reminder badge
The light maintenance look with a custom accent, on desktop and phone
Headline, message, launch date, contact line and look are set from the site settings

plugins.name: Mobile Action Bar
plugins.description: A bar at the bottom of the screen on phones with Call, Email, Directions and your own button, like Book a table. One tap for visitors, no JavaScript.
plugins.tagline: Call, email, directions and booking, one tap away on phones.
plugins.longDescription:
Mobile Action Bar adds a bar to the bottom of the screen for visitors on a phone, with the buttons a local business needs most: Call, Email, Directions and a main button of your own, such as Book a table or Order now.

Fill in only what you want to show. Your phone number becomes a tap-to-call button, your address opens in Google Maps, and your own button can point to any page. The labels come in English, Dutch, German and French, and your colour is used for the icons and the main button.

It is plain links and icons, with no JavaScript. The page gets a little space at the bottom so the bar never covers your content, and the bar respects the rounded corners and home indicator of modern phones. You can also show it on every screen, where it floats at the bottom like a small dock.

The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep your details. You can skip pages, such as your checkout.

screenshots.caption: On a phone: call, email, directions and your own button, always within reach.
Shown on every screen, it floats at the bottom like a small dock. Here in Dutch.
The settings: phone, email, address, your own button, language, colour and screens.

plugins.name: Opening Hours
plugins.description: Shows your opening hours as a neat table and a live "Open now · closes at 17:00" badge. Type [opening-hours] or [open-now] on any page.
plugins.tagline: Your opening hours as a neat table, with a live Open now badge.
plugins.longDescription:
Opening Hours shows when you are open, the way visitors want to know it: a clear table for the week, today highlighted, and a badge that says Open now · closes at 17:00, or Closed now · opens tomorrow at 09:00.

Type [opening-hours] on any page for the table, or [open-now] for the badge alone, and publish. You can also show the badge or the table in the footer of every page.

Enter each day like 09:00-17:00, add a lunch break with a second range, or write closed. Choose your time zone, so the badge is right for visitors abroad too, and a language for the day names: English, Dutch, German or French. A short note, such as Closed on public holidays, goes under the table.

The table is plain HTML and works without JavaScript. Whether you are open right now is worked out when a visitor looks, not when the page was published, by a few hundred bytes of script. The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep your hours.

screenshots.caption: A visit page with the week's hours, today highlighted, and the Open now badge.
In Dutch on a phone, on a Sunday evening: closed, and when you open again.
The settings: hours for each day, a note, your time zone, language and footer.

plugins.name: Promo Popup
plugins.description: One friendly popup for a sale, a newsletter or an event. Show it after a few seconds, on scroll or when someone is about to leave, and not again for days.
plugins.tagline: One friendly popup for a sale or newsletter. Never pushy.
plugins.longDescription:
Promo Popup shows one popup to your visitors: a sale, a newsletter, a workshop, a new product. Give it a title, a short text, an optional image and a button, and choose when it appears: after a few seconds, after scrolling down the page, or when a visitor is about to leave.

It is polite by design. Each visitor sees it once, and then not again for as many days as you choose, or only once per visit, or only ever once. Change the text and it counts as a new popup, shown again. It can sit in the middle of the screen or slide in small in a corner, and you can keep it off pages such as your checkout.

It uses the browser's own dialog, so Escape, the close button and screen readers all work, and animations are left out for visitors who prefer less motion. Whether a visitor has seen it is remembered in their own browser; nothing is sent anywhere and nobody is tracked.

The plugin asks for one permission, storage, to keep the popup.

screenshots.caption: A workshop invitation with an image and a button, in the middle of the screen.
Or small in the corner, where it does not get in the way of reading.
The settings: text, image, button, when to show it, how often, look and pages.

plugins.name: Reading Progress
plugins.description: A thin reading progress bar at the top of long pages, plus an optional back-to-top button. Pure CSS scroll-driven animation with a tiny JavaScript fallback.
plugins.tagline: A slim reading progress bar and a back-to-top button for long pages.
plugins.longDescription:
Reading Progress puts a thin bar across the top of every long page that fills as the reader scrolls, so they always know how much is left. Once they are half a screen down, a round back-to-top button fades in the corner and takes them back up with one click.

It needs no setup. Out of the box you get a 3 px rose bar and a button in the bottom right. Short pages that barely scroll get no bar. In the site settings you can pick your own colour, make the bar thin, medium or bold, move the button to the left, turn the button off, or skip pages by slug.

It is built to be light. The bar runs on a native CSS scroll-driven animation, so modern browsers do not run any code on scroll. Older browsers get the same result from a tiny inline script. There are no third-party requests, fonts or images: about 2 KB in total.

It is accessible by default. The bar is decorative and hidden from screen readers. The button is a real link with an accessible name, a 44 px target and a visible focus ring. It picks a white or dark arrow to stay readable on your colour, scrolls smoothly only for visitors who have not asked for reduced motion, and is hidden when printing.

The only permission it asks for is storage, to keep its settings. Refuse it and the plugin still works with the defaults.

screenshots.caption: Zero configuration: a slim rose bar at the top and a back-to-top button in the corner.
Close up: the bar tracks how far the reader is; the button fades in half a screen down.
Your colour, a bold 8 px bar and the button on the left.
Every option in Settings: colour, thickness, back-to-top button, its position and pages to skip.

plugins.name: Reading Time
plugins.description: Shows an estimated reading time, like "4 min read", under the first heading of every page, and keeps a per-page word count an editor can see in the site settings.
plugins.tagline: Shows readers how long a page takes, like "4 min read", under the title.
plugins.longDescription:
Reading Time counts the words on each page and shows an estimate like "4 min read" right under the first heading. Readers see at a glance how long a guide, article or case study will take before they start.

There is nothing to set up. With the default settings you get a small pill with a clock icon. It uses the page's own text colour, so it suits any theme. Only the prose in the article is counted: scripts, styles, navigation, footers and asides are skipped. The estimate is rounded up to whole minutes and is never less than one.

In Site settings you can set the reading speed (200 words a minute by default), change the label (for example to "minuten leestijd"), pick an accent colour, list pages to skip, such as home and contact, or switch to plain text that your theme styles itself. The panel also shows how many pages have been counted and which one is the longest.

The published page gets no JavaScript and makes no third-party requests. The badge adds under 600 bytes of inline CSS, and its clock icon is hidden from screen readers, so assistive technology reads just "4 min read". The label you type is escaped before it goes into the page.

The only permission it asks for is storage, to keep its settings and the per-page word counts. If you refuse it, every page still gets a reading time with the default settings.

screenshots.caption: Zero configuration: a quiet "3 min read" badge under the title, in the page's own colours.
Close-up with a custom accent colour. The clock is decorative; screen readers hear just the time.
Every option in Site settings: speed, label, style, accent colour and pages to skip.

plugins.name: Schema Markup
plugins.description: Adds JSON-LD structured data to every published page: your Organization or LocalBusiness (address, opening hours, phone), the WebSite, and a BlogPosting for posts, so Google can show rich results.
plugins.tagline: JSON-LD for your business, website and blog posts, ready for Google rich results
plugins.longDescription:
Schema Markup adds structured data to every published page, in the JSON-LD format Google, Bing and other search engines read. Visitors see nothing; search engines get a clear description of who you are and what each page is.

Describe your organization once in the site settings: name, logo, phone, email, address and social profiles. Choose Local business, Shop, Restaurant or Professional service to add opening hours such as "Mo-Fr 09:00-17:30" and a price range, which is what makes you eligible for local business results.

Every page also gets a WebSite entry. Blog posts, the pages whose address starts with blog or news, get a BlogPosting with the headline, description, social image, language, word count, author and publisher. The plugin takes these from the page itself, so there is nothing to fill in per post.

It works with no setup: the site name comes from your page titles and the site address from the canonical link. Every value is escaped, so nothing you type can break out of the script. It makes no external requests, adds no visible markup, and needs only the storage permission for its settings. If that permission is refused, it keeps working with the defaults.

screenshots.caption: A published blog post and the WebSite and BlogPosting data the plugin added to its head
A shop with address, opening hours, phone and social profiles, on every page

plugins.name: SEO Inspector
plugins.description: Checks every page when it is saved: title length, meta description, image alt text, headings, thin content and long URLs. Shows a 0-100 score and the warnings per page in the site settings.
plugins.tagline: A 0-100 SEO score and clear warnings for every page, checked on save.
plugins.longDescription:
SEO Inspector checks each page the moment it is saved and gives it a score from 0 to 100, with a plain list of what to fix.

It looks at what search engines and screen readers notice first: a missing or too short meta description, an SEO title that is too short or will be cut off in search results, images without alt text, pages with no h1 or more than one, skipped heading levels such as h2 followed by h4, thin content and long URLs.

All reports live in Site settings under SEO Inspector, worst page first, so you always know which page to fix next. The limits for thin content, title length and URL length are adjustable, and the defaults follow the usual rules of thumb.

It never changes a page and adds nothing to your published site: no scripts, no styles, no requests to anyone.

screenshots.caption: Every page with its score and warnings, worst first.
The panel in Site settings, with the thresholds you can adjust.

plugins.name: Social Share
plugins.description: Adds share buttons for X, LinkedIn, Facebook, WhatsApp, e-mail and copy link under your articles. Plain links and inline icons: no third-party scripts, no tracking.
plugins.tagline: Privacy-friendly share buttons under every article. No trackers.
plugins.longDescription:
Social Share adds a tidy row of share buttons under your articles: X, LinkedIn, Facebook, WhatsApp, e-mail and copy link.

Every button is a plain link with an inline icon. Nothing loads from Facebook, X or anyone else, so there are no third-party scripts, no cookies and no tracking. A reader's browser only talks to a network when the reader clicks its button.

It looks good straight away. Pick from four styles in the site settings: brand colours with labels, outlined, round brand icons, or minimal icons in your own accent colour. You can also change the heading, centre the row, switch off any network, and choose which pages show it, for example only pages under blog or news.

It is built to be accessible: descriptive labels for screen readers, a visible keyboard focus ring, a spoken "Link copied" confirmation, and no motion for readers who prefer reduced motion.

It asks for one permission, storage, to keep its settings. Refuse it and the plugin still shows the default buttons.

screenshots.caption: Share buttons under a journal article, in the default brand-colour style.
Close-up: X, LinkedIn, Facebook, WhatsApp, e-mail and copy link, all plain links with inline icons.
All options in the site settings: heading, style, accent colour, alignment and networks.
The round-icon style, centred, with a custom heading.

plugins.name: Table of Contents
plugins.description: Builds a linked table of contents from the h2 and h3 headings of a page, gives every heading an anchor id, and puts it at the top of the article, boxed or as a sticky sidebar. No JavaScript.
plugins.tagline: A linked table of contents for long pages, built from your headings.
plugins.longDescription:
Table of Contents reads the h2 and h3 headings of a page, gives each one a clean anchor id and puts a linked, nested list of them at the top of the article, in the same column as your text. Readers can see what a long page covers and jump straight to the part they came for. Every heading also gets a shareable link, like /guide#what-a-drawing-is-for.

It needs no setup. Pages with at least three headings get a quiet box titled "On this page" in your site's own fonts and colours. Short pages, the header and the footer are left alone. Headings that already have an id keep it, and duplicate headings get unique anchors.

Prefer it out of the way? Switch to the sticky sidebar style. On wide screens the list stays in the left margin while the reader scrolls, and on smaller screens it falls back to the box. You can also number the sections, list only h2 headings, change the title, pick an accent colour, set the minimum number of headings and skip pages by slug.

The published page gets no JavaScript and makes no third-party requests. The links are plain anchors, the styling is about 1.5 KB of inline CSS, and smooth scrolling only happens for visitors who have not asked for reduced motion. The markup is an accessible nav landmark with a label and visible focus styles.

The only permission it asks for is storage, to keep its settings. Refuse it and the plugin still works with the defaults.

screenshots.caption: Zero configuration: an "On this page" box at the top of the article, in the site's own type.
Sections and subsections, nested, each one a plain anchor link. No JavaScript.
Sidebar style: numbered, with a custom accent, and sticky in the margin while you read.
Every option in Settings: headings, minimum count, title, style, numbering, accent and skipped pages.

plugins.name: WhatsApp Chat
plugins.description: A floating WhatsApp chat button with a preset message, left or right placement, your own colour and optional opening hours. Accessible, CSS-only animation, no third-party scripts.
plugins.tagline: A floating WhatsApp button with a preset message and opening hours
plugins.longDescription:
WhatsApp Chat adds a round WhatsApp button to the corner of every published page. One tap opens a chat with your number, with a message already typed that the visitor can still change.

Place it bottom right or bottom left, keep WhatsApp green or use your own colour, and add a short label such as "Questions? Chat with us". On phones the label hides itself so the button never covers your content.

Optionally show the button only during opening hours: choose the days, the times and your time zone, and visitors outside those hours simply see no button.

It is built to be light and respectful: a plain link to wa.me, no WhatsApp scripts, no tracking and no third-party requests. The pulse and hover animations are pure CSS and switch off for visitors who prefer reduced motion. The button is a real, keyboard-focusable link with a clear accessible name and a contrast-checked icon.

It needs only the storage permission, for its settings.

screenshots.caption: A WhatsApp button with a short label in the corner of a live page
On a phone the label steps aside and only the round button remains
Number, preset message, label, position, colour and hours in the site settings
